## Summary
- Add first-class `/install` routing with `AGENT_INSTALL_PAT`-only execution and disabled memory/rubrics writes.
- Add the typed install target resolver and fork-backed prepare/publish helper for target GitHub mechanics.
- Keep target-specific install judgment in the `agent-install` prompt instead of adding an install lifecycle planner.
- Update install docs and focused coverage for route wiring, target resolution, helper behavior, and prompt boundaries.

## Verification
- `npm --prefix .agent run build`
- `node --test .agent/dist/__tests__/install-target.test.js .agent/dist/__tests__/install-fork-pr-cli.test.js .agent/dist/__tests__/install-fork-pr.test.js .agent/dist/__tests__/triage.test.js .agent/dist/__tests__/resolve-dispatch-cli.test.js .agent/dist/__tests__/extract-context-cli.test.js .agent/dist/__tests__/envelope.test.js .agent/dist/__tests__/rubrics.test.js`
- `env GITHUB_OUTPUT=/tmp/sepo-install-target-output REQUEST_TEXT='@sepo-agent /install https://github.com/foo/bar' node .agent/dist/cli/resolve-install-target.js`
- `git diff --cached --check`

Closes #300

| coding_workflow / generic | Prefer permissive command route parsing | pass | 7/7 | `/install` detection passes the full request through, while `resolve-install-target` accepts slug/URL forms and returns `missing`/`ambiguous` states. |

| coding_workflow / generic | Make user-facing automation idempotent | partial | 5/7 | Existing install PRs are reused and the branch is pushed, but the publish path returns the existing PR without updating title/body from the new body file. |
| coding_workflow / generic | Surface stateful failures | pass | 7/7 | Missing/mismatched prepare state blocks publish before push, with focused tests covering both failure modes. |
| coding_workflow / generic | Comment on accepted workflow stops | pass | 6/6 | Missing `AGENT_INSTALL_PAT` produces a concise visible blocked response instead of silently no-oping. |
| coding_workflow / generic | Separate diagnostics from continuity | pass | 7/7 | Install runs set `memory_mode_override: disabled`, `rubrics_mode_override: disabled`, and `session_policy: none`. |
| coding_workflow / generic | Make surgical changes | pass | 8/8 | The PR is broad but scoped to the linked #300 install-flow simplification, with lifecycle-planner behavior moved into the prompt/helper boundary rather than unrelated refactors. |

## Notes

- The implementation largely matches issue #300: route-specific authorization, `AGENT_INSTALL_PAT` isolation, typed target resolution, helper-owned fork/PR mechanics, no lifecycle planner, and prompt-owned target judgment.
- The main rubric gap is idempotent user-facing artifact handling for reused install PRs: the branch updates, but PR metadata can go stale.

## Findings

- **WARNING:** `publishInstallForkPr` does not update an existing install PR’s title/body on reuse. The prompt requires a fresh PR body with source revision, installed/skipped files, validation, and setup steps, and the docs say an existing install PR is reused. But in the reused path, the helper pushes `HEAD:${branch}` and immediately returns the old PR URL without calling `gh pr edit` or otherwise applying `bodyFile`/`title` to the existing PR. Evidence: [`publishInstallForkPr` reused branch](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/f2a051d3ee1b1432aa487f436960b4b2fba2461c/.agent/src/install-fork-pr.ts#L682-L697), prompt PR body contract at [`agent-install.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/f2a051d3ee1b1432aa487f436960b4b2fba2461c/.github/prompts/agent-install.md#L73-L94), and current reuse test only asserts no `pr create`, not body/title update.

## Final Rubric Verdict

PARTIAL

## Summary of PR/Issue

PR #301 implements issue #300 by simplifying the `/install` flow around a first-class route, install-only token isolation, a typed target resolver, and a deterministic fork/PR helper. The goal is to keep GitHub mechanics in helper code while leaving target-specific install judgment to `.github/prompts/agent-install.md`. The PR also updates docs and tests around route authorization, install target resolution, helper behavior, and prompt boundaries. Current PR head is `f2a051d3ee1b1432aa487f436960b4b2fba2461c`, with the `check` run passing; the PR is still draft.

## Review

The core implementation matches the linked issue direction, and the reviewers did not identify blocking defects. The independent review was `SHIP`; the rubrics review was `PARTIAL` due to one idempotency gap in reused install PR metadata.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Reused install PR metadata can go stale | WARNING | `publishInstallForkPr` pushes updates for an existing install PR, then returns without applying the fresh title/body file. That can leave source revision, validation, setup, or skipped-file details stale on reruns. |

## Progress

- `/install` is first-class and route-authorized, with `AGENT_INSTALL_PAT` isolated from normal auth paths.
- Memory and rubrics writes are disabled for install runs.
- The lifecycle planner was removed; prompt/helper ownership now matches issue #300.
- Existing inline comments and review threads are empty.
- No new inline comment was posted because the same metadata-staleness issue is already clearly covered in the current PR discussion by the rubrics review; no replies, minimizations, or thread resolutions were performed.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Reused install PR metadata can go stale</summary>

**Cause:** In [`publishInstallForkPr`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/f2a051d3ee1b1432aa487f436960b4b2fba2461c/.agent/src/install-fork-pr.ts#L682-L697), the `existingPr` branch returns immediately after pushing `HEAD:${branch}`. The fresh `title` and `bodyFile` validated earlier are only used on the new-PR path via `gh pr create --title ... --body-file ...` at [`L700-L715`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/f2a051d3ee1b1432aa487f436960b4b2fba2461c/.agent/src/install-fork-pr.ts#L700-L715), even though the prompt requires a current PR body with source revision, validation, and setup details.

**Candidate solutions:** Update the existing-PR path to run `gh pr edit <existingPr.number or url> --repo <target> --title <title> --body-file <bodyFile>` after the push succeeds, then return the reused PR result. Add regression coverage to the reused-PR test so it asserts metadata refresh, not just absence of `pr create`.

**Comments:** The positive review treated this as non-blocking, while the rubrics review flagged it as the only material gap under idempotent user-facing automation.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step

`FIX_PR`

The remaining issue is a small, concrete helper/test change that is safe for an automated fix-pr pass.

## Final Verdict

`MINOR_ISSUES`

## Action Items

- [ ] Refresh title/body metadata when `publishInstallForkPr` reuses an existing install PR, and add regression coverage for that path.

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
- PR #301 implements issue #300 by simplifying the `/install` flow around first-class route authorization, `AGENT_INSTALL_PAT` isolation, typed target resolution, and a deterministic fork/PR helper.
- The intended boundary is that helper code owns GitHub mechanics while `.github/prompts/agent-install.md` owns target-specific install judgment.
- The current head `7646fe2` also fixes the earlier reused-install-PR metadata issue by editing existing PR title/body after pushing.
- Review artifacts now agree the main design is sound; one remaining publish-time safety guard is still missing.

## Review
The rubrics review passes with no rubric-specific findings, while the code review flags one concrete publish-path edge case. This is not a broad design problem, but it is worth fixing before ship.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Publish can push the wrong worktree HEAD | WARNING | [`publishInstallForkPr`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/7646fe22359ea411496fb5db241272304041e744/.agent/src/install-fork-pr.ts#L665-L674) validates prepare-state metadata but never confirms the worktree is still checked out on the prepared install branch before pushing `HEAD:${branch}`. |

## Progress
- Prior reused-install-PR metadata warning is fixed in current head `7646fe2`.
- Current rubrics review is `PASS` with no rubric-specific follow-up.
- Existing inline comments and review threads were empty before synthesis.
- Posted one new inline comment on `.agent/src/install-fork-pr.ts:674`: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/301#discussion_r3270664582
- No replies, minimizations, or thread resolutions were performed.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Publish can push the wrong worktree HEAD</summary>

**Cause:** The helper validates that the worktree was prepared for the expected target, fork, token owner, and branch, but it does not validate the current checked-out branch before `runner.git(["push", ..., \`HEAD:${branch}\`])`. If the install prompt or release-copy work accidentally switches branches before publish, the helper can push that other `HEAD` to `agent/install-agent-infra`.

**Candidate solutions:** Add a current-branch guard after prepare-state validation and before push, returning a blocked result when the worktree is not on the expected install branch. Add a regression test that switches the prepared worktree to another branch before publish and asserts the helper blocks before pushing.

**Comments:** This is the only unresolved issue from the current review artifacts; it is small and localized to `.agent/src/install-fork-pr.ts` plus its tests.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
`FIX_PR`

The remaining issue is a concrete helper/test change that is safe for an automated fix-pr pass.

## Final Verdict
`MINOR_ISSUES`

## Action Items
- [ ] Add a publish-time current-branch guard before pushing `HEAD:${branch}`, with regression coverage for the wrong-branch publish case.
